title: Mechanistic machine learning links PI3K to Src-inhibitor effects in cardiac fibroblasts
summary: LogiMML, trained on high-content images of human cardiac fibroblasts, predicted that Src inhibition suppresses actin–myosin stress fibers through PI3K signaling. Follow-up PI3K inhibition reduced stress-fiber formation and procollagen I production in the fibroblasts, supporting the proposed pathway mechanism.
ai_technology: LogiMML, a logic-based mechanistic network coupled to ridge regression
organization: University of Virginia School of Medicine; and Brigham Young University

evidence.tested: LogiMML, trained on high-content images of human cardiac fibroblasts, predicted that Src inhibition suppresses actin–myosin stress fibers through PI3K signaling.
evidence.unknown: The validation is in vitro in primary human ventricular cardiac fibroblasts; it supports a pathway contribution to measured cell phenotypes, not therapeutic efficacy in an animal model or patients. The model's PI3K effect is described as partial.
evidence.ai_role: LogiMML fitted the relationship between high-content microscopy phenotypes and perturbations to an experimentally informed fibroblast signaling network, then predicted pathway mechanisms for pirfenidone and the Src inhibitor WH-4-023. Researchers tested the PI3K component of the Src-inhibitor prediction with PI3K inhibition in human cardiac fibroblasts.
